claims.text: Jeffrey Skilling resigned as CEO of Enron on August 14, 2001, citing personal reasons
Skilling's unexpected resignation was publicly announced on August 15, 2001, raising questions about Enron's financial health
Skilling was indicted on fraud charges in July 2002 related to Enron's accounting practices
Skilling was convicted on multiple counts of fraud and conspiracy on May 25, 2006

outcome.summary: Jeffrey Skilling resigned as Enron CEO in August 2001, months before the company's accounting fraud was exposed. He was later indicted and convicted on multiple counts of fraud and conspiracy in 2006, sentenced to 24 years in prison (later reduced to 14). Enron filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in December 2001, then the largest in US history.
